sentences.text: Both species share a skull feature where the squamosal and parietal bones meet at the posterior border of the supratemporal fenestra.
S. anatoceps was the first crocodyliform described from the Crato Formation in the Araripe Basin.
Researchers believe the holotype specimen was a desiccated carcass before burial and fossilization.
Susisuchus was likely restricted to a maximum size of 50 kg because larger bodies would have exceeded the structural limits of its high-walking posture.
Susisuchus was an extinct crocodyliform that lived in Brazil during the Early Cretaceous period, with fossils found in the Nova Olinda Member of the Aptian-age Crato Formation in northeastern Brazil.
The genus Susisuchus was named by Salisbury et al. in 2003 and is the only member of its family, Susisuchidae.
A second species, S. jaguaribensis, was named in 2009 based on fragmentary remains.
The remains of S. jaguaribensis were found about 115 km from the discovery site of S. anatoceps in the Lima Campos Basin.
A 2009 specimen from the Crato Formation was tentatively classified as cf. Susisuchus sp. based on unique fibula and leg bone proportions.
There are 5 recorded fossil occurrences of Susisuchus.
Susisuchus possesses a dorsal shield of osteoderms similar to those found in modern crocodilians.
Susisuchus was among the first mesoeucrocodylians to evolve a tetraserial paravertebral shield made of dorsal osteoderms.
A tetraserial paravertebral shield consists of four separate rows of osteoderms near the midline of the back.
Susisuchus has two rows of accessory osteoderms on either side of the main paravertebral shield.
The segmented paravertebral shield allowed Susisuchus greater lateral flexibility in its trunk.
The flexible shield likely enabled efficient lateral undulation swimming in Susisuchus.
If Susisuchus grew to a mass exceeding 50 kilograms, the forces encountered during upright walking may have been too large to be counteracted by the paravertebral shield.
Susisuchus is closely related to the genera Pachycheilosuchus and Isisfordia.
Susisuchus is placed outside the Eusuchia clade as its sister taxon, unlike its relative Isisfordia.
Susisuchus possesses amphicoelus vertebrae, meaning the ends of its vertebrae are concave.
The combination of amphicoelus vertebrae and a tetraserial shield is unique enough to define the family Susisuchidae.
Susisuchus is closely related to Pachycheilosuchus from Glen Rose, Texas, USA, and Isisfordia from Winton, Queensland, Australia.
Susisuchus lived from the Berriasian to the Aptian stages, between 143.1 and 113.2 million years ago.
